newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch NMB-Heller net up 23 percent.
newsitem.headline: Dutch NMB-Heller net up 23 percent.

text.p: Dutch factoring and financing group NMB-Heller Holding NV said on Wednesday 1996 net profit rose 23 percent to 61.6 million guilders from 50.1 million in the previous year.
This result was realised despite falling interest rates and strong competition, the 50-50 joint venture of Fuji Bank unit Heller International and the Dutch ING Group added.
"For 1997, a further growth of turnover and profits is expected," NMB-Heller said in a statement.
In 1996, turnover surged by 42.7 percent to some 23.5 billion guilders.
Turnover in the Netherlands grew by 14.7 percent to 11.7 billion guilders and German unit Heller Bank AG posted a turnover growth of 16.2 percent to six billion marks.
In Britain, NMB-Heller last year acquired all shares of factoring group TI-Heller Ltd.
The results of the French subsidiary Inter-Credit were negatively affected by the difficult economic situation and the bankruptcy of some of its clients.
NMB-Heller said its client base and turnover in Poland and the Czech Republic, where it started joint ventures in 1995, had grown rapidly.
The Czech joint venture O.B. Heller will open an outlet in Slovakia in the course of 1997, NMB-Heller said.
The company said it expected moderate turnover growth in the Netherlands and France this year but added that growth rates are expected to be higher in Germany and Britain.
In the Czech Republic and Poland continuous high turnover growth is expected, it added.
